Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: PekingSpades
Message:
fix(device-runtime): post-review round 10 — fs projection, list_dir lstat, fs_read numeric validation

Four findings.

P1 — capability-projection treated every filesystem tool as action=read +
pathPrefixes=['/']:
  Result: a user without any grant hit a "request read for /" UI even
  for fs_write/fs_edit/fs_delete/fs_history_restore; after they
  approved, the device runtime denied the call (it needs write). A
  scoped /repo grant + fs_index_status({subtree:'/repo'}) widened the
  request to '/' instead of using the actual subtree.

  Fix: per-tool action/path map in buildRequestedAction:
    - writeTools (fs_write, fs_edit, fs_delete, fs_history_restore) →
      action=write
    - subtreeTools (fs_index_status, fs_index_rebuild,
      fs_index_task_status) → pathPrefix = args.subtree ?? '/'
    - noScopeReadTools (fs_search) → pathPrefix='/'; runtime resolves
      against the caller's existing read prefixes, so this only kicks
      in when the caller has no fs grant at all
  Six new tests lock the contract; renamed buildRequestedAction → exported
  for testing.

P2 — list_dir leaked symlink-target metadata via fs.stat:
  /public/link → /secret/file under a /public read grant exposed the
  target's size and mtime; broken links were silently filtered (their
  existence is itself a side channel).

  Fix: lstat in listLegacy. Symlinks surface as kind:'symlink' with
  size:undefined; broken links are no longer skipped (kind:'symlink',
  link's own mtime). VfsNodeKind already had 'symlink' in the union.

P3 — fs_read accepted NaN/-1/1.5 for start_byte/end_byte/max_bytes:
  Bare asNumber pass-through let bad inputs hit vfs.readBytes →
  Buffer.alloc, surfacing as confusing "Invalid array length" /
  "out of range" errors instead of stable invalid_request.

  Fix: validateByteOffset + validatePositiveByteCount helpers mirroring
  validateOffset/validateLimit. Strict finite-integer + range checks
  bounded by ctx.cfg.maxReadBytes. Four new fs_read tests cover NaN,
  negative, non-integer, zero rejections.

Tests: device-runtime 112 (+5) / api 678 (+6 new projection tests). 5
pre-existing API failures (DB-dep) unaffected. Workspace build clean.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: PekingSpades
Message:
feat(stage 2): QQ webhook inbound (Ed25519 + URL verify + OQ2 gate)

webhook-signature.ts
  - Deterministic Ed25519 keypair from a botSecret (or clientSecret per
    OQ1 default) seeded into 32 bytes via UTF-8 repeat+truncate, same
    derivation as the QQ wiki Go reference + openclaw verifier.
  - Uses Node's built-in crypto.sign / crypto.verify (no new deps).
  - signEd25519UrlVerification(secret, plain_token, event_ts) →
    hex signature for op=13 reply.
  - verifyEd25519BusinessEvent(secret, signatureHex, timestamp, rawBody)
    — verifies the `X-Signature-Ed25519`/`X-Signature-Timestamp` headers
    against the raw HTTP body (G1 makes rawBody available).
  - extractSignatureHeaders handles lowercase + canonical-case + array
    header forms.

qq-account-config.ts
  - zod-validated {webhookInboundConfirmed, allowProactiveBestEffort,
    configuredUrlDomains}. Booleans must be `true`/`false` literals; the
    string "true"/"false" or numeric 0/1 are rejected to prevent silent
    truthy coercion.
  - Server-side hostname normalization: lowercases, strips
    scheme/path/query/fragment/port, drops empties, dedupes. Wildcards
    and bare IPv4 are rejected by zod refines.
  - readQqAccountConfig(account) returns a fully-defaulted record;
    isDashboardDomainAllowed(config, domain) is case-insensitive.

normalize.ts
  - normalizeQqC2cMessage / normalizeQqGroupAtMessage:
    QQ event payloads → InboundEnvelope with the address-encoding
    helpers. C2C uses c2c:{user_openid}; group uses
    gm:{group_openid}:{member_openid} so the same human in different
    groups doesn't collide on transport_addresses.external_id.
  - Group @-bot content stripping: heuristic regex drops a single
    leading <@bot> token + whitespace; Stage 4.5 will replace with the
    proper mentions[] driven parser.
  - Stores QQ-specific fields (message_type, message_scene,
    union_openid, group_openid) under raw/endpointMetadata for Stage 5
    (attachments) and Stage 7 (refIdx backfill).

inbound.ts
  - handleQqWebhook is now real:
    * op=13 → URL verification reply
    * op=0  → require rawBody + signature headers, verify, then check
              OQ2 gate (webhookInboundConfirmed must be === true, else
              200 ack-only with no emit) and dispatch C2C / GROUP_AT;
              GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE silently ignored; INTERACTION_CREATE
              on webhook is a warn-and-drop (QQ delivers it via WS).
    * other op → 200 ack-only (mis-routed WS opcode)
  - All response bodies use {op:12} HTTP_CALLBACK_ACK on success per
    wiki. Failures return descriptive {error:string} on 400/401/500.

Tests (42 QQ-specific + full IM suite 363 pass):
  - webhook-signature.test.ts: deterministic sign, sign/verify roundtrip,
    tamper rejection, bad-hex rejection, short-secret repeat, header
    extraction shapes.
  - qq-account-config.test.ts: defaults, string-bool rejection,
    wildcard/IP rejection, host normalization, passthrough.
  - normalize.test.ts: C2C + group encoding, missing-field returns null,
    leading @bot strip, raw/endpointMetadata preservation.
  - inbound.test.ts: op=13 signed reply, op=0 raw-body + signature +
    OQ2 gate transitions, all event types' dispatch paths.
